contents.text: Ben and I spent all day relaxing by the pool.

header.text: Some simple sentences have introductory phrases, but the introductory phrase is part of the predicate.

contents.text: In the winter, Ben usually wears his heavy coat.
Ben usually wears his heavy coat in the winter.

header.text: A compound sentence is made up of two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction such as and, but, or, or so.

contents.text: We saw the flash of lightning, and seconds later we heard a rumble of thunder.

header.text: A complex sentence is made up of an independent clause and a dependent clause. The dependent clause in a complex sentence usually begins with a subordinating conjunction or relative pronoun. Subordinating conjunctions include after, although, as, because, before, if, since, unless, until, when, and while. Relative pronouns include that, which, who, whom, or whose.

contents.text: If she ever gets the chance, Terri would love to visit the Egyptian pyramids.
During his trip to Italy, Tony visited the Trevi Fountain, which is in Rome.

header.text: A compound-complex sentence is made up of two or more independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses.

contents.text: After Samantha left work, she stopped at the bank, and then she went to the gym.

header.text: Sometimes a dependent clause in a complex or compound-complex sentence can interrupt an independent clause.

contents.text: Orcas that are kept in captivity often have bent dorsal fins.
